# Worked examples

Blank templates tell you what to fill in; they do not tell you what *good* looks like, or how much detail is expected. These are the same templates completed for one fictional company, so you can see the level of detail that makes an artefact defensible.

!!! tip "Deliberately imperfect"
    These examples include an amber board pack, a risk being tolerated,
    a control that was failing in practice, and an outstanding action
    past its owner. A worked example where everything is green teaches
    nothing.

## Meridian Health Analytics

**Meridian Health Analytics** is a fictional 340-person company selling
analytics software to NHS trusts and private healthcare providers in the UK
and EU.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Size** | 340 staff; ~£42m revenue |
| **Sector** | Health technology (B2B software) |
| **Markets** | UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Germany |
| **AI footprint** | 3 systems built in-house, 4 bought, 6 embedded in existing SaaS |
| **Regulatory exposure** | EU AI Act (deployer and provider), UK & EU GDPR, NHS DSPT |
| **Governance maturity** | Level 2 — documented, inconsistently applied |

Meridian is deliberately mid-size and imperfect. It has a governance
committee that meets but sometimes lacks quorum, an inventory that was
incomplete until a discovery sweep found six embedded AI features nobody had
registered, and one high-risk system — a triage prioritisation tool — that
is the reason its board started asking questions.
